name: Office of the Director of National Intelligence

summary.text: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence was established by the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (Public Law 108-458), signed December 17, 2004, following the 9/11 Commission's recommendation of a national intelligence director; its first director, John Negroponte, was sworn in on April 21, 2005 and the office began operations on April 22, 2005. The DNI heads the 18-member Intelligence Community, serves as principal intelligence adviser to the President, the National Security Council and the Homeland Security Council, and oversees the National Intelligence Program budget. On this site it appears through its 2025 Annual Threat Assessment, which stated that the intelligence community continued to assess that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon.

facts.claim: ODNI was established with enactment of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 on December 17, 2004 (Public Law 108-458); in February 2005 the President nominated John Negroponte as the first DNI and Lt. Gen. Michael Hayden as principal deputy, they took their oaths on April 21, 2005, and ODNI began operations on April 22, 2005.

facts.claim: The DNI serves as head of the Intelligence Community, a coalition of 18 agencies and organizations, and as principal advisor to the President, the National Security Council and the Homeland Security Council for intelligence matters related to national security; the DNI is appointed by the President with Senate consent and oversees the National Intelligence Program budget.

facts.claim: ODNI's 2025 Annual Threat Assessment (March 2025) stated that the intelligence community continued to assess that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon and that the Supreme Leader had not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003; DNI Tulsi Gabbard delivered that assessment to the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence on March 26, 2025.
